vocabulary.meaning_en: the desk at the airport where you show your ticket and give your bags
vocabulary.example: Go to the check-in desk first.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an official document you need to travel to other countries
vocabulary.example: Can I see your passport, please?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a large bag for clothes when you travel
give your bag to the airline to carry
vocabulary.example: How many suitcases are you checking in?
Place your bag on the scale.
Your bag is a bit too heavy.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the most a bag can weigh
vocabulary.example: It is over our weight requirement.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small bag you take into the plane with you
vocabulary.example: Put it in your carry-on bag.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the place where they check you and your bags
vocabulary.example: Take your laptop out at the security check.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a seat next to the window
vocabulary.example: I would like a window seat.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the card you need to get on the plane
vocabulary.example: Let me print your boarding pass.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the door where you get on the plane

vocabulary.example: Be at the gate one hour before departure.

vocabulary.meaning_en: travelling from one place to another

fine_lines.title: window seat vs aisle seat
fine_lines.explanation_ar: window seat = بجانب النافذة. aisle seat = بجانب الممر.
fine_lines.explanation_en: A "window seat" is next to the window. An "aisle seat" is next to the passage.

examples.sentence: I want a window seat to see the view.
An aisle seat is easy to get out of.

fine_lines.title: suitcase vs carry-on bag
fine_lines.explanation_ar: suitcase حقيبة كبيرة تُشحن. carry-on bag حقيبة صغيرة تأخذها معك داخل الطائرة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: A suitcase goes under the plane. A carry-on bag stays with you in the plane.

examples.sentence: My laptop is in my carry-on bag.

expressions.phrase: Can I see your passport, please?
expressions.meaning_en: The airline worker asks for your passport.
expressions.example: Can I see your ticket, please?
Thanks for flying with us today.

expressions.phrase: How long will you stay? / I'll be there for a week.
expressions.example: How long will you stay in Cairo? For two weeks.

expressions.phrase: How many suitcases are you checking in?
expressions.example: How many bags are you checking in? Two.

expressions.phrase: Your bag is a bit too heavy.
expressions.meaning_en: The bag is over the limit.
expressions.example: Sorry, your suitcase is too heavy.
I missed my bus. What should I do?

expressions.phrase: Is that okay? / Yes, that's fine.
expressions.meaning_ar: هل هذا مقبول؟ / نعم، لا بأس.
expressions.example: Can I take water? Is that okay?

expressions.phrase: How do I get to the gate?
expressions.example: How do I get to Gate 32?
Follow the signs to the exit.

expressions.phrase: Have a safe and happy journey!

grammar.title: Future: will for plans and facts
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم will للحديث عن المستقبل: How long will you stay? I'll be there for a week.
examples: How long will you stay in Tokyo?
I'll be there for a week.
I'll take this big book out.

grammar.title: too + adjective
grammar.explanation_ar: too + صفة = أكثر من المسموح أو اللازم (مشكلة).
grammar.explanation_en: "Too" + adjective = more than allowed or needed.
